stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-lem.fps.lau.justification: The two declarations jointly state exactly the two coefficient shifts in the blueprint. `mul_T_coeff` quantifies over `(a : LaurentPolynomial K) (n : ℤ)` and proves `(a * LaurentPolynomial.T 1) n = a (n - 1)`, matching `a · x = (a_{n-1})_{n ∈ ℤ}`. Likewise, `mul_T_neg_one_coeff` proves `(a * LaurentPolynomial.T (-1)) n = a (n + 1)`, matching `a · x^{-1} = (a_{n+1})_{n ∈ ℤ}`. The base-library definition identifies `LaurentPolynomial.T n` with `T ^ n`, so `T 1` and `T (-1)` represent the blueprint’s `x` and `x⁻¹`. The binder `[CommRing K]` agrees with the blueprint’s commutative-ring setting, and `LaurentPolynomial K` is the finitely supported family representation specified by the informal definition.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-lem.fps.lim.justification: The formal hypothesis `∀ k ≤ n, (PowerSeries.coeff k) f = if k = 0 then 1 else 0` exactly expresses the blueprint assumption “`[x^k] f = δ_{k,0}` for all `k ≤ n`,” using the informal definition of the Kronecker delta. Its conclusion `∀ k ≤ n, (PowerSeries.coeff k) (g * f) = (PowerSeries.coeff k) g` exactly matches “for any `k ≤ n`, `[x^k](g · f) = [x^k] g`.” The binders `{g f : PowerSeries K}` and `{n : ℕ}` represent the stated formal power series and natural-number bound, while `[CommRing K]` matches the section’s fixed commutative ring. Although `g` is an implicit rather than explicit binder, it remains universally quantified, so “for any `g`” is preserved.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-def.fps.f-s.justification: The formal definitions encode exactly the displayed coefficient formulas. `f_series'` has coefficient at `m` equal to `Ring.choose (n + ↑(m / 2) - 1) (m / 2)` when `Even m`, and `0` otherwise, which is precisely the FPS `∑ i, binom (n+i-1) i x^(2i)`. `g_series'` is `PowerSeries.binomialSeries K n`, whose library meaning is “the power series for `(1 + X) ^ r`,” matching `∑ j, binom n j x^j = (1+x)^n`. The binders `{K} [CommRing K] [BinomialRing K] (n : K)` provide the generalized binomial coefficients needed by both formulas. Although the blueprint mentions integers, rationals, reals, complexes, and more generally elements of a `ℚ`-algebra, allowing any commutative binomial ring is a mathematically broader setting rather than an added restriction, so it is faithful.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-def.sf.bk-f.justification: The forced predicates exactly encode the blueprint’s vertical adjacency conditions. `isForcedK` requires `T c = k` and a cell `c_below` with the same column, `↑c.1 + 1 = ↑c_below.1`, and value `k+1`; `isForcedKSucc` symmetrically requires a directly adjacent cell above with value `k`. The unmatched predicates also implement the stated left-to-right matching on a semistandard row: if there are `a` free k’s followed by `b` free (k+1)’s, `freeKCountUpTo ... > freeKSuccCount ...` selects the rightmost `a-b` k’s when `a>b`, while `freeKCount ... + freeKSuccCountUpTo ... ≤ freeKSuccCount ...` selects the leftmost `b-a` successors when `b>a`. Their explicit conjuncts `¬ isForcedK ...` and `¬ isForcedKSucc ...` restrict them to free cells. The formal binders use an arbitrary `AlgebraicCombinatorics.Tableau lam mu` rather than the blueprint’s “semistandard tableau,” and allow arbitrary skew shapes; this is a wider domain rather than an added hypothesis. On the blueprint’s semistandard tableaux, weak row increase ensures the relevant free k’s precede the free (k+1)’s, so the count formulas agree with the parenthesis algorithm.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-def.sf.fill.justification: The target adds the binder `{N : ℕ} → [inst : NeZero N]`, whereas the informal statement defines content for a filling with values in `[N]` and does not require `N ≠ 0`. This narrows the definition to positive `N`. The restriction enters through the dependency `SkewFilling`, whose signature also requires `[NeZero N]`, and through `skewYoungDiagram`, even though `NPartition.youngDiagram` and `Fin N` are meaningful for `N = 0`. Apart from that restriction, the body `fun ... f i => {c | f c = i}.card` exactly counts the cells in `Y(λ/μ)` satisfying `f(c) = i`, as required. To make it faithful, remove `[NeZero N]` from `SkewFilling`, use a skew-diagram definition valid for every `N` (as the dependency docstring itself recommends), and remove the corresponding binder from `fillingContent`.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-def.sf.row-.justification: The blueprint says to “Convert an SSYT of row partition shape $(n,0,\ldots,0)$ back to a multiset” by extracting “the entries of row $0$.” The target takes `hN : 0 < N`, `n : ℕ`, and `T : SymmetricFunctions.SSYT (SymmetricFunctions.NPartition.rowPartition N n hN)`, exactly an SSYT of that row shape; `hN` is required by the informal row-partition definition (“Requires $N>0$”). Its body defines `entries0` from `T.entries` at row `⟨0, hN⟩` and returns `weaklyIncreasingToSym n entries0`. That dependency constructs an element of `Sym (Fin N) n`, whose base-library meaning is an `n`-element multiset up to permutation. Thus the formal definition implements precisely the stated extraction and conversion, with no additional mathematically substantive hypothesis.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-lem.cancel..justification: The blueprint asserts a bijection between sign tuples and subsets of `[d]`, “sending each tuple `e` to the set … where `e_i = -1`.” Its definitions encode sign tuples as `Fin d → ZMod 2`, encode `[d]` as `Fin d`, and specify that residue `1` represents sign `-1`. The target `(d : ℕ) → (Fin d → ZMod 2) ≃ Finset (Fin d)` gives exactly such a bijection, with `toFun := signTupleToSubset`; that dependency has body `fun e => {k | e k = 1}`, exactly the specified subset. Its inverse has body `fun S k => if k ∈ S then 1 else 0`, and the two cited inverse laws establish the equivalence. `Finset (Fin d)` faithfully represents subsets because `Fin d` is finite, and there are no additional mathematical hypotheses.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-lem.det.des.justification: The target quantifies over every commutative ring and every 2×2 matrix: `∀ {R : Type u_1} [CommRing R] (A : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) R)`. Its equality is exactly the Desnanot–Jacobi formula: `A.det * (innerSubmatrix A).det` equals the product of the minors removing the first row/column and last row/column, minus the product of the two cross-minors. Here `0 : Fin 2` is the first index and `Fin.last 1` is the last index; `submatrixRemove` uses `Fin.succAbove`, so it genuinely removes the specified row and column. For a 2×2 matrix, `innerSubmatrix` has type `Matrix (Fin 0) (Fin 0) R`, correctly representing removal of both first and last rows and columns. `Matrix.det` is the Leibniz determinant required by the informal definition. Thus the declaration faithfully states that the Desnanot–Jacobi identity holds for all 2×2 matrices over a commutative ring.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-lem.fps.fg-.justification: The target adds the mathematically substantive binder `[inst : CommRing K]`, while the blueprint merely says “Let f, g ∈ K[[x]]” and none of the supplied informal definitions states that multiplication in `K` is commutative. The FPS operations require ring-like operations, but their formulas do not impose commutativity. Thus the formal theorem is restricted to commutative rings and is weaker than the unrestricted blueprint statement. This restriction enters through both the target binder and the dependency `PowerSeries.subst`, whose signature requires `[CommRing R]` and `[CommRing S]`. Otherwise the clauses correspond exactly: `PowerSeries.constantCoeff g = 0`, `∀ m < k, coeff m f = 0`, and `∀ m < k, coeff m (PowerSeries.subst g f) = 0` express the stated constant-term condition and the first-`k` coefficient claims. To make it faithful, either state in the blueprint that `K` is a commutative ring, or provide/use a composition operation under the weaker ring assumptions actually intended and weaken the target’s `CommRing K` binder accordingly.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-lem.fps.lim.justification: The formal binders exactly match the blueprint: `∀ {K} [CommRing K] {n : ℕ} {f g : PowerSeries K} (u v : Kˣ), ↑u = ↑v → (f ≡[x^n] g) → ...`. Here `PowerSeries.XnEquiv` is defined as `∀ m ≤ n, coeff m f = coeff m g`, matching agreement for every `m ∈ {0,1,…,n}`. The hypothesis `↑u = ↑v` expresses that the units are equal as underlying elements of `K`, and the conclusion `f.invOfUnit u ≡[x^n] g.invOfUnit v` is precisely that their formal inverses with respect to those units are x^n-equivalent. The `CommRing K` setting also agrees with the blueprint definitions.

stmt-algebraic-combinatorics-lem.sf.nipa.justification: The blueprint asserts that the forward and inverse maps give an equivalence `Nipat(λ, μ) ≃ SkewSSYT(λ/μ)`. The target has exactly this codomain and domain: `SymmetricFunctions.Nipat lam mu hlam hmu hcontained ≃ SymmetricFunctions.SkewSSYT { outer := ... lam ..., inner := ... mu ..., contained := ... }`. Its body uses `toFun := SymmetricFunctions.nipatToSSYT` and `invFun := SymmetricFunctions.ssytToNipat`, with both inverse laws supplied. The binders `hlam`, `hmu`, and `hcontained` merely encode that `lam` and `mu` are partitions with `μ ⊆ λ`, as required to form the skew shape `λ/μ`; they are not additional restrictions beyond the objects named in the blueprint.
